$meta.name: vinc-design
$meta.note: The source of truth for the Vinc 'Signal' design system. base = the homepage and web Vinc theme (Home · Signal); tenants/desktop = the desktop application (Deep Signal). Operated dark first: the runtime default is data-theme=dark, while the engine is light-first and emits :root=light, so the consuming shell pins dark itself. Derivation: imports/figma-variables-2026-07-19.json (mapped by hand from Figma). Monochrome since 2026-09-24: dark is neutral black and every accent is black, white or grey in both modes; only success, warning and danger keep a hue, plus the domain tint (a user toggle). The state notation (●◐○·≡≈) is kept alongside colour, never instead of it. Glow is for graph nodes only.
$meta.a11y: WCAG 2.2 AA. Only tokens verified at a body contrast of 4.5:1 or better may be used as text.

viewScene.note: Depth tiers for the View 3D mark, used only by the dark glow branch (app/src/surfaces/view3d.ts). This is the canonical copy; imports/figma-variables-*.json is only the record of the original import. Just three keys are consumed: fill, stroke and glowOpacity. glowRadius, edge and grid were removed on 2026-08-02 because no code read them (they were dead handles: changing the value changed nothing on screen). Values may be a {primitive} reference (resolved by gen_theme_ts.py). Monochrome since 2026-09-24. Verified by Vinc/scripts/gate_contrast.py

domainTint.note: Open-layer domain tint for the View marks (on by default since 2026-08-16; it shipped off and a hidden default read as a screen with a broken feature, see decision:topic-tint-ships-on). This is emphasis, not encoding: it is a user toggle in ViewPrefs, so it must never be the only way to tell two nodes apart. The hue is assigned by golden angle over the topics present on screen, so a topic does not keep its hue when the scope or the topic set changes; that instability is accepted because two topics landing on the same hue makes the feature do nothing, and a hash gave exactly that (measured: two pairs within 6 to 8 degrees across eight topics). Saturation and lightness are fixed here rather than in app code so the contrast floor is a token, not a literal: the lightness sits near the ink it replaces, which is what keeps the tinted mark readable in each mode. Consumed by app/src/view-tint.ts.

grain_50.$description: Light card surface, the top of the grain ramp

grain_100.$description: Light page background (the grain grey of the logo reference) · text on a CTA

grain_200.$description: Light alternating section band · muted surface

ink_900.$description: Cool near-black ink, body text in light mode. Pure black is forbidden

ink_400.$description: Captions and meta only (light). Forbidden for body text (the caption layer)

warn_bg.$description: Light warning background and chip only. Forbidden as text

win_close.$description: Hover on the titlebar close button. This is an operating-system convention (Windows), not a brand colour, so it does not change with the mode and sits on a different axis from danger: danger states a condition, this follows a window-control convention. The counterpart of the Figma Window collection (223:35)

d_bg0.$description: Dark page and application background, the deepest layer. Neutral black since 2026-09-24 (was a navy black)

d_bg1.$description: Dark surface · alternating section · panel base

d_bg2.$description: Dark card · left navigation · raised surface

d_text.$description: Dark body text (neutral ivory), 16.9:1 on d_bg0. Also the dark primary, focus and link: accents are monochrome since 2026-09-24

d_soft.$description: Dark secondary text, 8.3:1 on d_bg0 (AA ✓) · dark ring and info

d_mute.$description: Dark caption · meta · disabled, 5.9:1 / APCA Lc 40 on d_bg0. Forbidden for body text

d_warn_bg.$description: Dark warning background only. Forbidden as text

grain_300.$description: The floor for the light fade channel, APCA Lc 16.0. hairline (Lc 9.3) falls below the invisibility floor of 15, so it cannot be the faded colour of a graph line

brand_black.$description: Black logo on light backgrounds. Brand only.

brand_white.$description: White logo on dark backgrounds. Brand only.

gray_200.$description: Neutral line and mark shade: dark heavy edge and the near tier of the View 3D mark (11.8:1 / Lc 73 on d_bg0)

gray_400.$description: Dark node ring and cross-domain edge, APCA Lc 45.4 on d_bg0. A thin line is held to the fine-detail threshold (Lc 45), which d_mute (Lc 40.3) misses, so this is one step brighter

gray_500.$description: The main edge line. Dark 4.59:1 / Lc 31.7 · light 3.84:1 / Lc 62.0, the neutral that passes both gates in both modes

gray_600.$description: Cross-domain edge in light mode, 4.57:1 / Lc 67.5 on grain_100: one step darker than the main edge so the two stay apart without a hue

gray_700.$description: The floor for the dark fade channel, just above the APCA invisibility floor of Lc 15 (16.3). The fade channel is exempt from 3:1 but must never disappear entirely

gray_800.$description: Fill of the mid tier of the View 3D mark (depth impression; its ring d_soft carries the visibility)

motion.note: Curves and durations. The lime-design engine cannot emit this group (HUB-NOTES §5), so scripts/gen_motion.py injects it into the dist/ outputs during scripts/build_dist.py. Values are shared by every skin. ease-out: entrances, exits, small UI (caret, press, hover lift). ease-in-out: something already on screen moving to a new place. ease-drawer: large surfaces (sidebar column, document pane, sheets) — the macOS drawer curve. ease-settle: strong deceleration for menus, cards and the modal growth in app/motion.ts. dur-in/dur-out/dur-panel are read by app/motion.ts and view-bundle.ts at runtime.
